+use std::time;
+
+use serde_json as json;
+
+use hay::{SHERLOCK, SHERLOCK_CRLF};
+use util::{Dir, TestCommand};
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+#[serde(tag = "type", content = "data")]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+enum Message {
+    Begin(Begin),
+    End(End),
+    Match(Match),
+    Context(Context),
+    Summary(Summary),
+}
+
+impl Message {
+    fn unwrap_begin(&self) -> Begin {
+        match *self {
+            Message::Begin(ref x) => x.clone(),
+            ref x => panic!("expected Message::Begin but got {:?}", x),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn unwrap_end(&self) -> End {
+        match *self {
+            Message::End(ref x) => x.clone(),
+            ref x => panic!("expected Message::End but got {:?}", x),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn unwrap_match(&self) -> Match {
+        match *self {
+            Message::Match(ref x) => x.clone(),
+            ref x => panic!("expected Message::Match but got {:?}", x),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn unwrap_context(&self) -> Context {
+        match *self {
+            Message::Context(ref x) => x.clone(),
+            ref x => panic!("expected Message::Context but got {:?}", x),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn unwrap_summary(&self) -> Summary {
+        match *self {
+            Message::Summary(ref x) => x.clone(),
+            ref x => panic!("expected Message::Summary but got {:?}", x),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct Begin {
+    path: Option<Data>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct End {
+    path: Option<Data>,
+    binary_offset: Option<u64>,
+    stats: Stats,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct Summary {
+    elapsed_total: Duration,
+    stats: Stats,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct Match {
+    path: Option<Data>,
+    lines: Data,
+    line_number: Option<u64>,
+    absolute_offset: u64,
+    submatches: Vec<SubMatch>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct Context {
+    path: Option<Data>,
+    lines: Data,
+    line_number: Option<u64>,
+    absolute_offset: u64,
+    submatches: Vec<SubMatch>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct SubMatch {
+    #[serde(rename = "match")]
+    m: Data,
+    start: usize,
+    end: usize,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+#[serde(untagged)]
+enum Data {
+    Text { text: String },
+    // This variant is used when the data isn't valid UTF-8. The bytes are
+    // base64 encoded, so using a String here is OK.
+    Bytes { bytes: String },
+}
+
+impl Data {
+    fn text(s: &str) -> Data { Data::Text { text: s.to_string() } }
+    fn bytes(s: &str) -> Data { Data::Bytes { bytes: s.to_string() } }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct Stats {
+    elapsed: Duration,
+    searches: u64,
+    searches_with_match: u64,
+    bytes_searched: u64,
+    bytes_printed: u64,
+    matched_lines: u64,
+    matches: u64,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct Duration {
+    #[serde(flatten)]
+    duration: time::Duration,
+    human: String,
+}
+
+/// Decode JSON Lines into a Vec<Message>. If there was an error decoding,
+/// this function panics.
+fn json_decode(jsonlines: &str) -> Vec<Message> {
+    json::Deserializer::from_str(jsonlines)
+        .into_iter()
+        .collect::<Result<Vec<Message>, _>>()
+        .unwrap()
+}
+
+rgtest!(basic, |dir: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    dir.create("sherlock", SHERLOCK);
+    cmd.arg("--json").arg("-B1").arg("Sherlock Holmes").arg("sherlock");
+
+    let msgs = json_decode(&cmd.stdout());
+
+    assert_eq!(
+        msgs[0].unwrap_begin(),
+        Begin { path: Some(Data::text("sherlock")) }
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        msgs[1].unwrap_context(),
+        Context {
+            path: Some(Data::text("sherlock")),
+            lines: Data::text("Holmeses, success in the province of detective work must always\n"),
+            line_number: Some(2),
+            absolute_offset: 65,
+            submatches: vec![],
+        }
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        msgs[2].unwrap_match(),
+        Match {
+            path: Some(Data::text("sherlock")),
+            lines: Data::text("be, to a very large extent, the result of luck. Sherlock Holmes\n"),
+            line_number: Some(3),
+            absolute_offset: 129,
+            submatches: vec![
+                SubMatch {
+                    m: Data::text("Sherlock Holmes"),
+                    start: 48,
+                    end: 63,
+                },
+            ],
+        }
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        msgs[3].unwrap_end().path,
+        Some(Data::text("sherlock"))
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        msgs[3].unwrap_end().binary_offset,
+        None
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        msgs[4].unwrap_summary().stats.searches_with_match,
+        1
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        msgs[4].unwrap_summary().stats.bytes_printed,
+        494
+    );
+});

+rgtest!(notutf8, |dir: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    use std::ffi::OsStr;
+    use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
+
+    // This test does not work with PCRE2 because PCRE2 does not support the
+    // `u` flag.
+    if dir.is_pcre2() {
+        return;
+    }
+    // macOS doesn't like this either... sigh.
+    if cfg!(target_os = "macos") {
+        return;
+    }
+
+    let name = &b"foo\xFFbar"[..];
+    let contents = &b"quux\xFFbaz"[..];
+
+    // APFS does not support creating files with invalid UTF-8 bytes, so just
+    // skip the test if we can't create our file.
+    if !dir.try_create_bytes(OsStr::from_bytes(name), contents).is_ok() {
+        return;

+    cmd.arg("--json").arg(r"(?-u)\xFF");

+    let msgs = json_decode(&cmd.stdout());

+    assert_eq!(

+    assert_eq!(
+        msgs[1].unwrap_match(),
+        Match {
+            path: Some(Data::bytes("Zm9v/2Jhcg==")),
+            lines: Data::bytes("cXV1eP9iYXo="),
+            line_number: Some(1),
+            absolute_offset: 0,
+            submatches: vec![

+    let msgs = json_decode(&cmd.stdout());
+
+    assert_eq!(
+        msgs[1].unwrap_match().submatches[0].clone(),
+        SubMatch {
+            m: Data::text("Sherlock"),
+            start: 56,
+            end: 64,
+        },
+    );
+});

+#[macro_export]
+macro_rules! rgtest {
+    ($name:ident, $fun:expr) => {
+        #[test]
+        fn $name() {
+            let (dir, cmd) = ::util::setup(stringify!($name));
+            $fun(dir, cmd);
+
+            if cfg!(feature = "pcre2") {
+                let (dir, cmd) = ::util::setup_pcre2(stringify!($name));
+                $fun(dir, cmd);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[macro_export]
+macro_rules! eqnice {
+    ($expected:expr, $got:expr) => {
+        let expected = &*$expected;
+        let got = &*$got;
+        if expected != got {
+            panic!("
+printed outputs differ!
+
+expected:
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+{}
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+got:
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+{}
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+", expected, got);
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[macro_export]
+macro_rules! eqnice_repr {
+    ($expected:expr, $got:expr) => {
+        let expected = &*$expected;
+        let got = &*$got;
+        if expected != got {
+            panic!("
+printed outputs differ!
+
+expected:
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+{:?}
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+got:
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+{:?}
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+", expected, got);
+        }
+    }
+}

+use hay::SHERLOCK;
+use util::{Dir, TestCommand};
+
+// This tests that multiline matches that span multiple lines, but where
+// multiple matches may begin and end on the same line work correctly.
+rgtest!(overlap1, |dir: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    dir.create("test", "xxx\nabc\ndefxxxabc\ndefxxx\nxxx");
+    cmd.arg("-n").arg("-U").arg("abc\ndef").arg("test");
+    eqnice!("2:abc\n3:defxxxabc\n4:defxxx\n", cmd.stdout());
+});
+
+// Like overlap1, but tests the case where one match ends at precisely the same
+// location at which the next match begins.
+rgtest!(overlap2, |dir: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    dir.create("test", "xxx\nabc\ndefabc\ndefxxx\nxxx");
+    cmd.arg("-n").arg("-U").arg("abc\ndef").arg("test");
+    eqnice!("2:abc\n3:defabc\n4:defxxx\n", cmd.stdout());
+});
+
+// Tests that even in a multiline search, a '.' does not match a newline.
+rgtest!(dot_no_newline, |dir: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    dir.create("sherlock", SHERLOCK);
+    cmd.args(&[
+        "-n", "-U", "of this world.+detective work", "sherlock",
+    ]);
+    cmd.assert_err();
+});
+
+// Tests that the --multiline-dotall flag causes '.' to match a newline.
+rgtest!(dot_all, |dir: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    dir.create("sherlock", SHERLOCK);
+    cmd.args(&[
+        "-n", "-U", "--multiline-dotall",
+        "of this world.+detective work", "sherlock",
+    ]);
+
+    let expected = "\
+1:For the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock
+2:Holmeses, success in the province of detective work must always
+";
+    eqnice!(expected, cmd.stdout());
+});
+
+// Tests that --only-matching works in multiline mode.
+rgtest!(only_matching, |dir: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    dir.create("sherlock", SHERLOCK);
+    cmd.args(&[
+        "-n", "-U", "--only-matching",
+        r"Watson|Sherlock\p{Any}+?Holmes", "sherlock",
+    ]);
+
+    let expected = "\
+1:Watson
+1:Sherlock
+2:Holmes
+3:Sherlock Holmes
+5:Watson
+";
+    eqnice!(expected, cmd.stdout());
+});
+
+// Tests that --vimgrep works in multiline mode.
+rgtest!(vimgrep, |dir: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    dir.create("sherlock", SHERLOCK);
+    cmd.args(&[
+        "-n", "-U", "--vimgrep",
+        r"Watson|Sherlock\p{Any}+?Holmes", "sherlock",
+    ]);
+
+    let expected = "\
+sherlock:1:16:For the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock
+sherlock:1:57:For the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock
+sherlock:2:57:Holmeses, success in the province of detective work must always
+sherlock:3:49:be, to a very large extent, the result of luck. Sherlock Holmes
+sherlock:5:12:but Doctor Watson has to have it taken out for him and dusted,
+";
+    eqnice!(expected, cmd.stdout());
+});
+
+// Tests that multiline search works when reading from stdin. This is an
+// important test because multiline search must read the entire contents of
+// what it is searching into memory before executing the search.
+rgtest!(stdin, |_: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    cmd.args(&[
+        "-n", "-U", r"of this world\p{Any}+?detective work",
+    ]);
+    let expected = "\
+1:For the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock
+2:Holmeses, success in the province of detective work must always
+";
+    eqnice!(expected, cmd.pipe(SHERLOCK));
+});
+
+// Test that multiline search and contextual matches work.
+rgtest!(context, |dir: Dir, mut cmd: TestCommand| {
+    dir.create("sherlock", SHERLOCK);
+    cmd.args(&[
+        "-n", "-U", "-C1",
+        r"detective work\p{Any}+?result of luck", "sherlock",
+    ]);

+    let expected = "\
+1-For the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock
+2:Holmeses, success in the province of detective work must always
+3:be, to a very large extent, the result of luck. Sherlock Holmes
+4-can extract a clew from a wisp of straw or a flake of cigar ash;
+";
+    eqnice!(expected, cmd.stdout());
+});

-|wd: WorkDir, mut cmd: Command| {
-    wd.create(".not-an-ignore", "foo\n/bar");

-    // First, get a baseline without applying ignore rules.

-    assert_eq!(lines, paths(&[
-        "bar/test", "baz/bar/test", "baz/baz/bar/test", "baz/foo",
-        "baz/test", "foo", "test",
-    ]));
-
-    // Now try again with the ignore file activated.
-    cmd.arg("--ignore-file").arg(".not-an-ignore");

pr.title: feat: add tclsh, wish, and expect shebang detection for Tcl syntax
pr.body:
## Summary

Adds `first_line_match` to the Tcl sublime-syntax definition so bat automatically detects Tcl scripts by their shebang line (`#!/usr/bin/tclsh`, `#!/usr/bin/wish`, `#!/usr/bin/expect`).

## Why this matters

bat recognizes `.tcl` files but not Tcl scripts that use shebangs without extensions. Expect scripts (`#!/usr/bin/expect`) and Wish scripts (`#!/usr/bin/wish`) are common in automation and GUI tooling but get no syntax highlighting from bat today.

## Changes

- `assets/patches/Tcl.sublime-syntax.patch`: Adds `first_line_match: ^\#!.*\b(tclsh|wish|expect)\b` to the bundled Tcl syntax definition. The regex matches tclsh, wish, and expect in any shebang path (`/usr/bin/`, `/usr/local/bin/`, `env` wrappers).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Added feature entry.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt -- --check`: pass
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: pass
- `cargo test --locked`: pass
- Patch dry-run verified: `patch --strip=0 --dry-run < patches/Tcl.sublime-syntax.patch` succeeds

Fixes #3513

This contribution was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code).

issue.title: Multi-file output
issue.body:
This issue proposes a design which would allow users to emit multiple files from a single Typst project. The main goal of this work is to enable emitting web sites with multiple pages, but the design enables further use cases. The feature would initially be guarded behind a feature flag, similarly to HTML export.

## Design

Currently, Typst supports four export formats spread across two targets: The formats PDF, PNG, and SVG are backed by the paged target and the HTML format has its own target.

This design introduces a new format and target called `bundle`. When this target is selected (from the CLI via `-f bundle`), multiple output files can be created from a single Typst file/project, all emitted to one output directory.

The design centers around the `document` function. Currently, this function can only be used in set rules. The function is extended to be directly callable. A single call to the `document` function results in one output file within the output directory.

The `document` function gains six new parameters:

- `path: string | path` (required): This parameter designates the path in the output directory of the document. It may contain interior slashes, which result in nested directories. The extension of the path is used to infer the format.

- `body: content` (required): The content that is processed to produce the file.

- `format: "pdf" | "png" | "svg" | "html" | auto` (optional): The export format. If `auto` or omitted, inferred from the path.

- `ppi: int | auto` (optional): Defines the default PPI (pixels per inch) used when rastering things. Initially, this would be used for raster export. In the future, it may also be used to define the PPI for raster effects in PDF export or for image recoding in PDF export.

- `pages: array | auto` (optional): The pages to output for paged documents. The array may contain integers indicating single pages and pairs (arrays of length two) of integers defining ranges.

- `pdf: dictionary` (optional): PDF-specific options, which includes `standard: string | auto`, and `tagged: bool | auto`. This property supports folding. We might want to split up `standard` into `version` and `standards`. This was discussed before, but not decided. If we do so, it should be split up in the CLI as well.

These configuration parameters mirror the document options exposed in the CLI (`--ppi`, `--pages`, `--pdf-standard`, `--no-pdf-tags`), with format-specific options in a dictionary, and options that may apply to multiple formats top-level. This extends the existing mapping between `document.date` and `--creation-timestamp`. Notably, we only expose export options, not environment parameters such as `--root` or `--font-path`.

In addition to the `document` function, a new `asset` function is introduced. This function can be used to emit a file whose contents are a raw string or bytes, in no particular format.

The existing experimental `target` function (guarded behind the `html` feature) returns `"bundle"` when the bundle target is selected. When within a `document`, it returns the appropriate target for that document.

### Use Cases

- Building a multi-page web site:

  ```typ
  #document("index.html")[
    #title[Home]
    - #link(<blog>)[Go to blog]
  ]

  #document("blog/index.html", title: "Laurenz's Blog")[
    #title[Blog]
    My blog!!!
  ] <blog>
  ```

- Producing a secondary file alongside the main file:

  ```typ
  #document(
    "slides.pdf",
    pdf: (standard: "a-2b"),
    [...],
  )

  #context asset(
    "speaker-notes.json",
    json.encode(query(<note>).map(it => it.value)),
  )
  ```

- Producing multiple files from the same content. In principle, this feature can be very powerful for producing varied versions of the same content, with differeng style or state configuration, e.g. a paper + slides, or two versions of a document with terms in different languages. In practice, many such use cases would initially be obstructed by how introspection would behave in multi-file export. See the "Limitations" sections for more details.

- Setting defaults for export options for single-file export:
  ```typ
  #set document(pdf: (standard: "ua-1"))
  ...
  ```

### Details

- Different documents can observe each other's contents through introspection. For introspection purposes, the whole bundle is one large output that is iterated on, rather than each document iterating separately. This enables various cross-document introspection use cases. In particular, documents could be labelled and linked to as far as this is supported by the specific export targets. The same holds for cross-document links.

- A document inherits styles from where it is placed:
  ```typ
  #set text(red)
  #document("main.pdf", [This is red])
  ```

- Top-level content is not allowed in the bundle target, i.e. this is an error when exporting a bundle:
  ```typ
  Top-level content!
  #document("main.pdf")[...]
  ```
  An exception to this would be spaces, parbreaks, and content that vanishes during realization (e.g. metadata, which shows as empty content regardless of the target) as these may naturally arise from formatting.

- Nested documents or assets are not allowed, i.e. this is an error:
  ```typ
  #document("main.pdf", document("other.pdf", [...]))
  ```
  In theory, this could be useful (particularly assets in documents, e.g. when emitting an image or data file used by a document in HTML export), but it's not clear whether this is semantically appropriate. Moreover, care would need to be taken to iteratively discover all nested document/assets elements. If this is considered desirable, it could be added later.

- Duplicate documents/assets with the same path are an error.

- PNG/SVG documents which result in more than one file require a pattern in the path name (as in the CLI).

- In the CLI, bundle output must be explicitly enabled with `-f bundle` and emits a directory of files. The directory output overwrites existing colliding files on disk, but does not delete unrelated files in the output directory. `typst watch` serves multi-file output with the live reloading server known from HTML export. Files are served from memory, so unrelated files in the output directory on disk are not served.

## Limitations

As mentioned above, I would like to support cross-document introspection, as it unlocks many useful features like cross-linking, cross-HTML-page navs and outlines, etc. However, for some use cases such as reusing the same content across multiple deliverables, this might be undesirable:

```typ
#show: it => {
  document("paper.pdf", it)
  state("slides").update(true)
  // Heading numbering is not reset here ...
  document("slides.pdf", it)
}

...
```

That said, similar things can already happen within a document (see e.g. https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/1841). Forbidding cross-document introspection generally seems like an unsuitable solution. It would severely limit the usefulness of the feature. Rather, I believe a more general mechanism that can be used both within and across documents is necessary. However, this is considered out of scope of the work on multi-file export.

## Unresolved questions

Should CLI options or `document` parameters take precedence? Is a difference being made between parameters configured via set rule in single file export versus parameters configured via direct arguments in bundle export?

Currently, a non-`auto` `document.date` takes precedence over the CLI's creation timestamp. However, I think it would be more useful if the document could specify a default export setting (a "preferred rendition" in XMP terms), with the CLI still having the option to override it. We might want to change the behavior here.

In particular, something like `set document(format: "png")` could be nice, but should imo be overridable.

## Alternatives

I have considered one primary alternative: Instead of producing any kind of document with the `document` function, we could have per-format elements, `pdf`, `png`, `svg`, and `html`. The `pdf`, and `html` elements would take on the role of the existing modules and absorb their definitions. This would be a minor breaking changes as the module -> element change would be observable, but normal usage such as `html.elem` or `pdf.attach` would continue to work as usual.

Upsides of this alternative:
- Format-specific export options could be cleanly exposed as properties on these types instead of all of them having to be fitted into dictionaries passed to per-format arguments on the `document` function.
- Only one place where each format exists: As a top-level binding that both creates such a document and exposes format-specific definitions. With the document design, we have both the top-level `pdf` module and the `document.pdf` field for PDF-specific document settings.

Downsides of this alternative:
- Pollution of the global scope, and potential for collisions, in particular if we might gain additional export formats such as plain text or Pandoc AST; how would the plain text document element be called? That said, formats that require custom definitions would need a module either way.
- Larger API surface with duplicated arguments for path and cross-format options. More annoying to set a default for such options, e.g. `#set document(pages: ((1, 5), 3))` would need to become three separate set rules for `pdf`, `png`, and `svg`.
- Conceptually an output file and a `document` have a 1-1 relationship, so using the same element has a certain elegance to it. Things like `set pdf(standard: "ua-1")` would need to behave similarly to `set document(..)`.
- The `svg` element could be mistaken for a function that embeds an SVG. To an extent, the same holds for the existing `pdf` module, but a bit less so as it's a module rather than an element.
- To me, the document-centered design seems more coherent with the rest of Typst. Elements like `image` or `bibliography` also abstract over multiple internal formats, rather than each format having its own element. The `document` element would follow this pattern.
- No natural way to set the default export format (unlike `set document(format: "png")`).

Another option would be to keep multi-file export as an HTML-specific thing (`html.document`/`html.page` + `html.asset`) if it's not considered useful enough for other targets. This was the initial idea when starting work on HTML, but upon discovering the potential for a generalization I very much started to like the idea of supporting this as a general mechanism.

## Prior art
- https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/4174
- https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/5512
issue.author: laurmaedje

pr.title: Bundle export
pr.body:
This pull request implements a new experimental export target that can emit multiple files from a single Typst project. The implementation mostly follows the design laid out in https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/7735.

The new export target is primarily useful for multi-page websites, but is not limited to that. You can create bundles containing any combination of HTML pages, PDFs, PNGs, SVGs, and arbitrary assets.

The primary motivation to ship this new target now is to use it in the ongoing work on porting the Typst documentation to Typst. However, it's also a big step in generally making HTML export more practically useful.

### Example

```bash
typst compile main.typ --format bundle --features bundle,html
```

```typ
#document("index.html", title: "Home")[
  #title()
  - #link(<blog>)[Go to blog]
]

#document("blog.html", title: "Blog")[
  #title()
  Welcome to my blog!

  ...

  This blog also exists as a
  #link(<blog-pdf>)[single PDF].
] <blog>

#document("blog.pdf", title: "Blog")[
  ...
] <blog-pdf>

#asset(
  "favicon.ico",
  read("images/favicon.ico", encoding: none),
)
```

In the example, we create two HTML documents: A home page and a blog. The home page links to the blog through a label link. Typst's built-in linking mechanism natively supports cross-document links and resolves the correct relative paths for you. The bundle also contains a PDF version of the blog, which is linked from the HTML version. In practice, you could now share the content between the HTML and PDF version by storing it in a variable and using it in both. This is omitted here for brevity. Finally, the bundle contains an icon asset for the website. In this case, we're providing the asset's data by reading a file from disk. Alternatively, it's also possible to generate asset data from within Typst (e.g. via a function like `json.encode`).

### Scope

Compared to the design issue, this is a _slightly_ scoped down version. Specifically, for now, I omitted the `ppi`, `pages`, and `pdf` parameters to `document`. Instead, export of individual documents respects the usual CLI parameters. In principle, I still want to expose these configuration options at the Typst level, but it's not blocking for landing the work itself and also not necessary for the docs work. Moreover, to make CLI settings and in-document settings interact cleanly, a few things need sorting out first.[^1]

[As mentioned in the issue](https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/7735#issuecomment-3908841853), I've also decided to accept that introspections are always global to the bundle for the time being. Often, this is exactly what you want, but in some cases, it's unwieldy. I don't think there's a simple clean "fix" for that. Rather, improving this will be more of a long-term process of evolving the introspection subsystem.

### Notes

The history is carefully crafted with `jj` :), so if you want to take a look at what's changed / how it's implemented, I invite you to read the commits in isolation.

### Linked issues

Closes https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/7735

[^1]: Primarily that `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is not perfectly handled at the moment. It behaves exactly like `--creation-timestamp` while in reality it should behave more like if the system clock happened to be it at its timestamp. I'll open a separate issue about that.

pr.title: Expose baselines for box and block
pr.body: Needed for #7895. Fixes #4796 (which might also address https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/7319#issuecomment-3498996342), #5855. Partially addresses https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/493. Boxes and blocks will now propagate the baseline of what's inside them - usually text or math - allowing them to properly align with their surrounding text / math. For this to work, text and math content now expose their baselines. For paragraphs, the baseline will be set to that under the first line of text. For math equations, the global baseline will be set to the baseline of the first row. And for content with more than one paragraph / equation, the baseline of the first one will be used. With that, several little annoyances when using `box` shall be gone. This means that: - Boxed inline equations will no longer be vertically shifted compared to non-boxed equations (#4796). You can now peacefully use `box($a x + b y = 10 - c z$)` to ensure that pesky long inline equation won't break across lines. - Same for any boxed text whatsoever. - Which implies you can now add a stroke (or use other `box` effects) around the boxed text, and it will now remain aligned! For blocks, for now, the only meaningful change is when a `block` is used inside an equation: it will now be properly aligned with the rest. For example, this is how `$ #block($y$) + y $` currently looks like: And this is how it will now look like: In the future (in #7895), block baselines will also be used for list marker alignment. In addition, `box(scale[Text])` will also use the correct baseline after the scaling **with `reflow: true`**. However, `box(rotate[Text])` will stay as it is today regardless of `reflow: true` as it is not yet very clear where the baseline should go after, say, a 180-degree rotation of a paragraph. ## Configuration Despite all the goodies listed above, it's possible the old behavior is still desired. In that case, `box(baseline: ...)` now accepts new values (defaulting to `auto`): - `box(baseline: bottom)` ensures text aligns with `bottom` of the box - **this was the previous default behavior.** - `box(baseline: top)` and `box(baseline: horizon)` also allow moving the baseline to the top or middle of the box. Note that `box(baseline: 5pt)` (to shift the baseline by that height compared to where it normally is) is still supported, and both options can be specified simultaneously through a **dictionary:** `box(baseline: (at: bottom, shift: 5pt))`. This is a **breaking change** if you're reading `context box.baseline` as this will now always return a dictionary. ## TODO - [x] Address remaining tests.

issue.title: Feature: --install flag to auto-install macOS apps to /Applications
issue.body:
## Feature Request

### Problem

After building a macOS app with `pake`, I must manually:
1. Open/mount the `.dmg` file
2. Drag the `.app` to `/Applications`
3. Unmount the DMG volume
4. Delete the `.dmg` installer

This is repetitive, especially during iterative development or when packaging multiple apps.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `--install` CLI flag that automates the entire post-build installation on macOS:

```bash
pake https://example.com --name "MyApp" --install
```

When `--install` is passed on macOS with a DMG target, the CLI will:
1. Mount the DMG via `hdiutil attach`
2. Copy the `.app` bundle to `/Applications` (replacing any existing version)
3. Unmount the volume via `hdiutil detach`
4. Remove the installer DMG

### Behavior

- **Opt-in**: Defaults to `false`, no change to existing behavior
- **macOS-only**: Only activates when `platform === 'darwin'` and `fileType === 'dmg'`
- **Graceful failure**: If installation fails, the DMG is preserved and an error message is shown
- **Visible in help**: Listed as a top-level option (not hidden)

### Implementation

I have a working implementation ready — PR incoming.

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [x] I'm willing to submit a PR!
issue.author: chindris-mihai-alexandru

pr.title: feat: add --install flag to auto-install macOS apps to /Applications
pr.body:
## Summary

- Add a new `--install` CLI flag that automatically installs built macOS apps to `/Applications` and removes the installer DMG after a successful build
- Eliminates the manual mount → drag → unmount → delete workflow for every `pake` build on macOS

Closes #1143

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `bin/types.ts` | Add `install: boolean` to `PakeCliOptions` |
| `bin/defaults.ts` | Default `install: false` |
| `bin/helpers/cli-program.ts` | Register `--install` CLI option (visible in help) |
| `bin/builders/BaseBuilder.ts` | Add `installDmgToApplications()` method + call site after build success |
| `tests/unit/cli-options.test.ts` | Add test for `--install` option registration |

## How it works

When `--install` is passed on macOS with a DMG target:

1. Mounts the DMG via `hdiutil attach`
2. Copies the `.app` to `/Applications` (replaces existing if present)
3. Unmounts via `hdiutil detach`
4. Removes the installer DMG

On failure, the DMG is preserved and an error is logged.

## Usage

```bash
pake https://example.com --name "MyApp" --install
```

## Design decisions

- **Opt-in only** — defaults to `false`, zero impact on existing workflows
- **macOS-only** — guarded by `IS_MAC && fileType === 'dmg'` (future Linux/Windows support could follow separately)
- **Graceful degradation** — if install fails, the DMG remains and an error message points to it
- **Uses `execa` directly** — avoids `shellExec` which is tied to `npmDirectory` as cwd
- **Visible in `--help`** — not hidden, since it's a user-facing quality-of-life feature

## Testing

- Unit test added for option registration (all 3 tests pass)
- Manually tested end-to-end: built and auto-installed LinkedIn and NoteBookLM apps to `/Applications` successfully

issue.title: Feature request: integrate custom, complete Symfony Console scripts
issue.body:
It's possible to include [simple CLI scripts into Composer's `scripts`/`scripts-descriptions` list](https://getcomposer.org/doc/articles/scripts.md#writing-custom-commands).
It's also possible to [point static methods/functions to run as complex-ish scripts](https://getcomposer.org/doc/articles/scripts.md#defining-scripts).
Lastly, under the hood, Composer uses the (great) Symfony Console library.

Thus, is there any chance it's possible to include complete Symfony Console scripts into the main list of scripts a project uses, without having to duplicate command names and descriptions into `composer.json`?

I see it's possible to include custom commands from plugins, but what about doing that directly from the main project? It's an overshoot to create a whole plugin to include commands to manage a single project (but it still looks better than the current flow of having a separate executable for that lol).

What I'm thinking is something like a `scripts-folder` config entry which will import all classes found under it into the project's composer executable, much like `scripts` does with CLI commands. The end result is being able to seamlessly see our (complex) custom scripts when running `composer list`, including the description and help content configured in a subclass of `\Symfony\Component\Console\Command\Command`.

Example:
I'm writing some i18n scripts to extract/upload/download translations, and that's best done from a CLI tool such as Symfony Console, which allows for processing of arguments, options, and console I/O. In the meantime, we already have a bunch of one-liners as Composer scripts (such as clear DB cache, compile frontend, migrations work) which work great being defined directly in `composer.json`.

pr.title: US phone numbers
pr.body:
This implements the rules for the North American Numbering Plan (NANP). It does not generate numbers including so-called "easily recognizable codes" which are used for various special services and not assigned to geographic regions, for example 911 (emergency), 411 (directory), 511 (traffic information) or 800 (toll-free).

Toll-free numbers can be generated with `tollFreePhoneNumber()`.

Fixes #588

issue.title: Suggestions for potential improvements for `PHPMailer::setLanguage()`
issue.body:
While writing tests for the logic involved in localizing the error messages, I came across a number of oddities which _may_ benefit from some tweaks to improve things.

**_Note: I'd be happy to make the changes I'm suggesting here. Just wanted to allow for discussion before sending in a PR._**


### Observation 1: Language code is case-sensitive
```php
// This works:
$mail->setLanguage('nl');

// This doesn't:
$mail->setLanguage('NL');
```

In a number of other places in the library, the code is very deliberately case-tolerant.

#### Proposal

It would only be a small tweak to make the `setLanguage()` method case-tolerant for the `$langCode` passed and may improve usability.


### Observation 2: ISO 639-1 multi-level: no fall back to "parent" language when available
```php
// This works:
$mail->setLanguage('nl');

// This doesn't:
$mail->setLanguage('nl_NL'); // "PHP" way of writing the code
$mail->setLanguage('nl-NL'); // Iso way of writing the code
```

For a few languages, there are multiple translation files available for variants of the language. For most languages this is not the case.

#### Proposal

When the `$langCode` is passed as "multi-level" and no translation is found for the specified variant, the localization currently falls back to English, while when a translation _is_ available in the "parent" language, it may be more appropriate to fall back to that translation.

So, when `nl_NL` would be passed, `nl` would be used when `nl_NL` can't be found and `nl` **is** available. The fall back to English would then only happen when neither `nl_NL` nor `nl` is available.



### Observation 3: ISO 639-1 multi-level: underscore versus dash

While for this library, underscore separators for multi-level language files are expected, the documentation talks about ISO 639-1 language codes, which, when multi-level, are expected to use a dash as separator.

#### Proposal

It would only be a small change to support both for the `$langCode` input, but again, may improve usability a little.



### Observation 4: Available language file `sr_latn` can never be used

There is a language file available for `sr_latn` (Serbian, latin script). However, this language code would never pass the regex validation of the `$langCode`, so this file is effectively useless.

#### Proposal

Either remove the translation file or adjust the regex to allow for loading it.
issue.author: jrfnl

pr.title: PHPMailer::setLanguage(): various fixes + add tests for localization
pr.body:
Fixes #2418 (and could only be pulled no after #2449 was merged as otherwise the tests would fail on PHP 5.5)

## Commit details

### PHPMailer::setLanguage(): make return value consistent

The return value of the method was inconsistent as it could return `true` even when the requested language was not loaded/set.

Previously, the method would:
* Return `false` when a `$langcode` was matched against the regex, but the file couldn't be loaded.
* Return `true` in all other cases, including when a `$langcode` other than `'en'` was passed, but it didn't match the regex, which meant that effectively the requested language was ignored and English was loaded anyway, but the function would still return `true`.

This has now been changed to:
* Return `true` when the requested language was loaded, whether `'en'` or another language.
* Return `false` when the requested language wasn't loaded and the language defaulted to English.

Related to #2418 (https://github.com/PHPMailer/PHPMailer/issues/2418#issuecomment-876265100)

### PHPMailer::setLanguage(): match language codes case-insensitively

For "language code - country code" locale notations, it is common for the "country code" part to be provided in uppercase, like `pt_BR`.

The method currently did not allow for that correctly. The regex check would accept the language code, but then fail to find the file on *nix based systems as the file names are all in lowercase and non-Windows file systems are generally case-sensitive. Which means that in effect, the method, ended up falling back to the default language (English).

The change in this commit makes the handling of the provided `$langcode` case-tolerant.

Note: the language code used in the file names for the language files is still expected to always be lowercase, including for language files in custom paths!

Related to #2418 - observation 1

### PHPMailer::setLanguage(): fix "lang_country" codes do not fall back to "lang"

When the  `$langCode` is passed as "language code - country code" and no translation is found for the specified country variant, the localization would automatically fall back to English, even when there was a viable translation available in the "parent" language, i.e. just based on the _language code_.

This commit changes the logic in the `PHPMailer::setLanguage()` method for when a "lang-country" code is passed.
It will now try and find a "lang-country" file first, if not found, it will try to find a file for just the "lang" and only if that could also not be found, it will fall back to English.

Related to #2418 - observation 2

Includes using named subpatterns in the regex to make the regex self-documenting.

Includes removing a commented out line of code which is superseded anyway.

### PHPMailer::setLanguage(): allow for "lang(_script)?(_country)?" codes

Language codes which were "language-script" based were not accepted by the regex used, which meant that the `sr_latn` script could never be loaded.

After discussion in #2418, it was decided to support "script" in a language code and to support it like so:
```
2-character language code [_] optional 4-character script code [_] optional 2-character country code
```

This combines the annotation forms of the following known standards:
* https://unicode-org.github.io/cldr-staging/charts/37/summary/root.html
* https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E23824_01/html/E26033/glset.html
* http://www.loc.gov/standards/iso639-2/php/code_list.php

This means that all of the below codes will now pass the language code validation:
```
sr
sr_latn
sr_rs
sr_latn_rs
```

But not:
```
sr_rs_latn
```

This commit applies the above change and also adjusts the "language code fall back" logic to take language codes with a script code into account.
Note: if the requested full "language-script-country" code is not available, "language-country" will take precedence over "language-script" for the fallback logic to find the appropriate translation file.

Related to #2418 - observation 4

### Tests: introduce dedicated tests for text localization

So far, the methods related to text localization - `PHPMailer::setLanguage()`, `PHPMailer::getTranslations()` and `PHPMailer::lang()` - did not have dedicated tests.

The test file this commit introduces, tests all aspects of these methods, including the changes introduced in response to #2418 and #2419, as well as documents the current behaviour of the methods for specific, outlier situations.

### PHPMailerTest: remove setLanguage() test

... which wasn't actually testing anything at all.

issue.title: Sender troubles in mailSend
issue.body:
Following this conversation https://github.com/PHPMailer/PHPMailer/discussions/3281
I've noted that the Sender logic here

https://github.com/PHPMailer/PHPMailer/blob/360ae911ce62e25e11249f6140fa58939f556ebe/src/PHPMailer.php#L2059-L2070

This is problematic, for two reasons:
The use of `sendmail_from` is not innocuous for non-Windows systems. Non-Windows systems cannot make use of `sendmail_from` but despite this, PHPMailer is bringing a functionality they don't have unnecessarily (enabling Sender).

I think we need to give this a second thought, but there is a second, bigger problem: enabling Sender has caused a major outage in several WordPress installations after 6.9. The idea of returning sender by default was mine because this is the best way to achieve an easier pass on DMARC for most setups (obviously some setups will struggle in the process, but this was expected). 

But there was an issue I described here https://github.com/PHPMailer/PHPMailer/discussions/3281, that for some reason, users without Sender could send email, and adding the `Sender` they could not and this made 0 sense to me.

I'm sending a PR to explain the solution.
issue.author: SirLouen

pr.title: Fixing troubles with mailSend and Sender enabled
pr.body:
Fixes #3282

Here is the problem: 
If the users already had defined the `sendmail_path` we were adding again to params the `-f` when the Sender was specified. 

This provoked a double sender (one from params and one from the sender path)

This patch simply check if the `-f` has been already set to avoid setting it again. 

About the Testing, it has been a little more complex than I expected
The problem here is that `sendmail_path` is `PHP_INI_SYSTEM` so it's impossible to modifiy this in runtime, so the only way to modify it is through the `php.ini` or passing the parameter to the PHPUnit binary run as I explain below.

I was checking the previous tests like `testMailSend` assuming that they were right as they were setting 
```php
ini_set('sendmail_path', '/usr/sbin/sendmail -t -i ');
```

But this is basically not doing anything as this cannot be set. 

The only way to execute the test with a different `sendmail_path` is through running something like this:

```
php -d sendmail_path="/usr/sbin/sendmail -t -i -frpath@example.org" ./vendor/bin/phpunit --filter  testMailSendWithSendmailParams
```

On the other side `sendmail_from` can be set as its not a `PHP_INI_SYSTEM` parameter. 

Note that the logic is very interesting in:

https://github.com/PHPMailer/PHPMailer/blob/360ae911ce62e25e11249f6140fa58939f556ebe/src/PHPMailer.php#L2059-L2070

Because adding a `sendmail_from` , enables the Sender in L2062 (regardless if the `setFrom` is `true` or not and then the L2064 validates the condition. This was the reason here https://github.com/PHPMailer/PHPMailer/discussions/3281 enabling it, despite being a non-Windows parameter, was changing the course of action (and this is why I thought it was a Poltergeist 🤣 because, how was it possible, that `sendmail_from` was doing something if the PHP docs explicitely said that this was a Windows-only parameter?). I reviewed the whole mail code in PHP and Sendmail server to only find that the problem was here...

This fix is somewhat time-sensitive to be rolled out in a new PHPMailer version because I need to send the patch downstream for next WP 6.9.1 release with the next version of PHPMailer to fix everyone's problems.
pr.author: SirLouen

issue.title: Allow extensions to output raw HTML
issue.body:
In a project I have created a custom extension of the `Parsedown` class that overrides the `Parsedown::blockFencedCodeComplete()` method to add "compile time" syntax highlighting to fenced code blocks. This worked pretty well in 1.6.4 and earlier releases. Since the element text that is created contains HTML (to apply the classes for the syntax highlighting), I intentionally left out the call to `htmlspecialchars()` in my overridden method. This is the resulting markup for an example fenced code block: ```html 
// baz.php

<?php

$foo = "bar";
``` With the 1.7.0 release though this broke because now the call to `htmlspecialchars()` doesn't seem to happen in the single element methods but rather in `Parsedown::element()` where every element is passed through. This is the markup I get now: ```html 
<span class="hljs-comment">// baz.php</span>

<span class="hljs-meta"><?php</span>

$foo = <span class="hljs-string">"bar"</span>;
``` My question is: with the latest changes, is there a way to restore the previous behavior? Don't get me wrong, I know sanitation is a serious topic and I think the changes are the right way to go. I just want to disable them for fenced code block in a project where I have complete control over the markdown passed through Parsedown.

issue.title: `loadTableIndexes()` includes LOB indexes with `NULL` column names, causing `strpos()` deprecation on PHP `8.1+`.
issue.body:
### Description

Oracle creates internal LOB indexes for CLOB/BLOB columns. These indexes have no entry in `USER_IND_COLUMNS (COLUMN_NAME is NULL)`. 

The `loadTableIndexes()` method in `src/db/oci/Schema.php` does not exclude them, causing `NULL` to propagate into `quoteColumnName()`  and `quoteSimpleColumnName()`.

- PHP `7.4`: Bug exists silently (`strpos(null, ...`) returns `false` without warning).
- PHP `8.1+`: 4 deprecation warnings: `strpos():` Passing `null` to parameter 1 ($haystack) of type string is deprecated at `Schema.php` lines 521, 524, 530, 568.


### Package version

2.0

### PHP version

8.1+
issue.author: terabytesoftw

pr.title: `loadTableIndexes()` includes LOB indexes with `NULL` column names, causing `strpos()` deprecation on PHP `8.1+`.
pr.body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Is bugfix?    | ✔️
| New feature?  | ❌
| Breaks BC?    | ❌


LOB indexes are internal structures (Oracle FAQ: "Which Views Can I Query to Find Out About a LOB Index?") only `*_INDEXES` and `*_LOBS` views list them,  `*_IND_COLUMNS` does not.  This causes `NULL` column_name on `LEFT JOIN`.

https://docs.oracle.com/cd/A91202_01/901_doc/appdev.901/a88879/adl06fa7.htm
pr.author: terabytesoftw

issue.title: Add support for BOM-signed env files
issue.body:
Hi!
I was working on a Laravel project that has a .env file.
But I faced an error that says:
`The environment file is invalid!`
`Failed to parse dotenv file due to an invalid name. Failed at [﻿APP_NAME].`

After some time for debugging, I realized the problem is come from encoding of the file!
The encoding of the .env file is [UTF8 BOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byte_order_mark)

In this [example files](https://github.com/hosni/tmp/tree/master/github.com/vlucas/phpdotenv/add-support-for-BOM-signed-env-files) you will see two files named `.env-UTF-8` and `.env-UTF-8-with-BOM`. They almost contains the same data, but `.env-UTF-8-with-BOM` starts with the UTF8 BOM, causing the parse error.

![image](https://github.com/hosni/tmp/blob/master/github.com/vlucas/phpdotenv/add-support-for-BOM-signed-env-files/.env-UTF-8.png?raw=true)

![image](https://github.com/hosni/tmp/blob/master/github.com/vlucas/phpdotenv/add-support-for-BOM-signed-env-files/.env-UTF-8-with-BOM.png?raw=true)

### How did happen?
I'm using linux as OS, but well it seems that when you add a text file in Visual Studio in windows, it adds the UTF8 BOM by default. I generated the second file that has to BOM using the Windows Explorer contextual menu "New File".

issue.title: [Feature Request] dedicated secrets file
issue.body:
### Describe the feature request

Rather than only having the option for `auth.token = <value>` (e.g. `auth.token = "thisismysecret"`) in the config, it would be ideal to have the option to say `auth.token_file = <path>`. (e.g., `auth.token_file = /var/lib/secrets/frp_token`.) The token secrets can then be loaded from those files by frp during initialization.

Putting a secrets file in a dedicated location is a useful standard for segregating secrets in their own directory, thus reducing the likelihood of mistakes when configuring file system permissions & file scope. It also reduces the likelihood of leaks if, e.g., someone is committing their configuration into version control / git (such as is de facto necessary in some workflows, such as NixOS).

pr.title: support multiple subjects in oidc ping
pr.body:
Validate the subject in an oidc ping against a list of logged in subjects.

This resolves the issue that multiple connected FRP clients with different OIDC clients result in a failing ping. The ping would fail because the subject in memory would be the value of the last logged in FRPC.

This change also changes the constructor of OidcAuthVerifier to take a TokenVerifier interface. This will not change production behavior, but makes testing easier because we can inject a mock verifier during testing.

Resolves: #4466

issue.title: add option to UseNumber() in gin.Context.BindJSON()
issue.body:
When receiving a json object with number values and calling `context.BindJSON()` (or `context.Bind()`), the numbers will be unmarshalled to `float64` values. If needed, this can be switched to unmarshalling into `int` by using `json.Decoder.UseNumber()`. However, `BindJSON()` doesn't give this control. This should be added somehow:
- maybe a global switch, though this doesn't give per-request control.
- maybe an additional parameter or `...` parameter

issue.title: With RedirectFixedPath enabled, the request execution panics when a 404 is expected
issue.body:
## Description

When a request to a path doesn't match any registered patterns and the `RedirectFixedPath` flag is set to true, the request execution panics (invalid node type). This is the line throwing the panic: https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/blob/v1.7.7/tree.go#L851 

If the panic is commented, everything seems to work as expected with the exception of the test `TestTreeInvalidNodeType`.

## How to reproduce

Add this function to the `gin_integration_test.go` file

```
func TestRedirectFixedPath(t *testing.T) {
	router := Default()

	router.RedirectFixedPath = true

	router.GET("/aa/aa", func(c *Context) { c.String(http.StatusOK, "/aa/aa") })
	router.GET("/:bb/aa", func(c *Context) { c.String(http.StatusOK, "/:bb/aa") })

	ts := httptest.NewServer(router)
	defer ts.Close()

	testRequest(t, ts.URL+"/aa/aa", "", "/aa/aa")
	testRequest(t, ts.URL+"/bb/aa", "", "/:bb/aa")

	testRequest(t, ts.URL+"/aa", "404 Not Found") // this request makes the router panic
}
```

## Expectations

The router should return a 404

## Actual result

The router panics and the client (curl) returns

```
curl: (52) Empty reply from server
```

## Environment

- go version: 1.17.3
- gin version (or commit ref): 1.7.7
- operating system: linux

``` fish
  function __fzf_ctrl_r
    set -l query (commandline|string trim)
    if test -z $query
      set query ''
    else
      set query "-q $query"
    end

    history | eval (__fzfcmd) +s +m --tiebreak=index --toggle-sort=ctrl-r  $query | read -l out
    and commandline $out
    commandline -f repaint
  end

pr.title: Strip the '+' and '-' characters when copying parts of a diff to the clipboard
pr.body:
- **PR Description**

This makes it easier to copy diff hunks and paste them into code. We only strip the prefixes if the copied lines are either all '+' or all '-' (possibly including context lines), otherwise we keep them. We also keep them when parts of a hunk header is included in the selection; this is useful for copying a diff hunk and pasting it into a github comment, for example.

A not-quite-correct edge case is when you select the '--- a/file.txt' line of a diff header on its own; in this case we copy it as '-- a/file.txt' (same for the '+++' line). This is probably uncommon enough that it's not worth fixing (it's not trivial to fix because we don't know that we're in a header).

Fixes #3859.
Fixes #4511.

--- a/pkg/gui/controllers/patch_explorer_controller.go
+++ b/pkg/gui/controllers/patch_explorer_controller.go
@@ -1,8 +1,11 @@
 package controllers
 
 import (
+	"strings"
+
 	"github.com/jesseduffield/gocui"
 	"github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/pkg/gui/types"
+	"github.com/samber/lo"
 )
 
 type PatchExplorerControllerFactory struct {
@@ -295,13 +298,49 @@ func (self *PatchExplorerController) CopySelectedToClipboard() error {
 	selected := self.context.GetState().PlainRenderSelected()
 
 	self.c.LogAction(self.c.Tr.Actions.CopySelectedTextToClipboard)
-	if err := self.c.OS().CopyToClipboard(selected); err != nil {
+	if err := self.c.OS().CopyToClipboard(dropDiffPrefix(selected)); err != nil {
 		return err
 	}
 
 	return nil
 }
 
+// Removes '+' or '-' from the beginning of each line in the diff string, except
+// when both '+' and '-' lines are present, or diff header lines, in which case
+// the diff is returned unchanged. This is useful for copying parts of diffs to
+// the clipboard in order to paste them into code.
+func dropDiffPrefix(diff string) string {
+	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(diff, "\n"), "\n")
+
+	const (
+		PLUS int = iota
+		MINUS
+		CONTEXT
+		OTHER
+	)
+
+	linesByType := lo.GroupBy(lines, func(line string) int {
+		switch {
+		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "+"):
+			return PLUS
+		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "-"):
+			return MINUS
+		case strings.HasPrefix(line, " "):
+			return CONTEXT
+		}
+		return OTHER
+	})
+
+	hasLinesOfType := func(lineType int) bool { return len(linesByType[lineType]) > 0 }
+
+	keepPrefix := hasLinesOfType(OTHER) || (hasLinesOfType(PLUS) && hasLinesOfType(MINUS))
+	if keepPrefix {
+		return diff
+	}
+
+	return strings.Join(lo.Map(lines, func(line string, _ int) string { return line[1:] + "\n" }), "")
+}
+
 func (self *PatchExplorerController) isFocused() bool {
 	return self.c.Context().Current().GetKey() == self.context.GetKey()
 }

issue.title: Discard changes can be very slow

**Describe the bug**

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Select a decent amount of files (for example a package in node_modules that you don't need anymore) 
2. Press **d** to discard 

**Expected behavior**
The UI should not lock up. Ideally this operation should be quick but if this is a limitation of git then I would like the operation to happen in the background or at least get some indication telling me that something is happening.

**Version info:**
_Run `lazygit --version` and paste the result here_

**Additional context**

pr.title: Improve performance of discarding many files
pr.body:
When selecting a directory containing many changed files, or when range-selecting many changed files, and then discarding them, this could be so slow that lazygit appeared to hang; especially since there was no UI feedback (e.g. a spinning status message).

This PR improves the performance greatly by batching the individual git calls into a single one if possible. It still doesn't add UI feedback though, hoping that the operation is now fast enough that it isn't needed.

While we're at it, we fix a bug that would cause "Discard unstaged changes" to discard more than just the visible files when filtering by path.

Fixes #4581.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/pkg/model/anchors.go
@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+package model
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+
+	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
+)
+
+func resolveAliasesExt(node *yaml.Node, path map[*yaml.Node]bool, skipCheck bool) error {
+	if !skipCheck && path[node] {
+		return errors.New("circular alias")
+	}
+	switch node.Kind {
+	case yaml.AliasNode:
+		aliasTarget := node.Alias
+		if aliasTarget == nil {
+			return errors.New("unresolved alias node")
+		}
+		path[node] = true
+		*node = *aliasTarget
+		if err := resolveAliasesExt(node, path, true); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		delete(path, node)
+
+	case yaml.DocumentNode, yaml.MappingNode, yaml.SequenceNode:
+		for _, child := range node.Content {
+			if err := resolveAliasesExt(child, path, false); err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+func resolveAliases(node *yaml.Node) error {
+	return resolveAliasesExt(node, map[*yaml.Node]bool{}, false)
+}

issue.title: scrape: Allow to disable end-of-run staleness marker injection for targets
issue.body:
### Use case

Suppose a project uses `scrape` package as a library in a cluster where targets are sharded across a number of instances. When a new instance joins the cluster, some portion of targets will typically be handed over to that new instance. The previous owning instance of a target that moved will attempt to inject staleness markers at the end of the scrape loop run (after delay of ~2 intervals). If out-of-order ingestion is enabled, writing staleness markers will succeed and results in occasional gaps in metrics.

[Grafana Alloy](https://github.com/grafana/alloy) faces the above [issue](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/issues/249) in practice. 

### Proposal

Expose a method on scrape manager that allows users to disable end-of-run staleness for user-specified targets. 

In above scenario, users of the `scrape` package will be able to detect that given target has moved to another instance and ensure that there are no unnecessary staleness markers written by the previous owning instance.

More generally, giving users control over when the staleness markers injection should or should not happen, can allow to implement more use cases correctly and with fewer data issues.
issue.author: thampiotr

issue.title: [RW2] Type and unit labels not applied when using Prometheus Agent
issue.body:
Hi! Thanks a lot to the Prometheus team for adding the new `type-and-unit-labels` feature!  

## Related PR
While testing it, i noticed some differences in behavior depending on the Prometheus mode.  

This behavior was tested after applying the changes from [#17329](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17329).  
While the improvement works correctly in standard Prometheus mode, the following results were observed when using the `agent` mode (details below).

---

##  Observed behavior

### Case 1 - Prometheus scrapes targets directly
Everything works as expected - the `__type__` label appears in the resulting metrics.

**Prometheus config**
```yaml
global:
  scrape_interval: 15s
  scrape_timeout: 10s
  evaluation_interval: 15s

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'node-exporter'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['test-node-exporter:9100']
    relabel_configs:
      - source_labels: [__address__]
        regex: '(.*):(.*)'
        target_label: instance
        replacement: '${1}'
      - source_labels: [__address__]
        regex: '(.*):(.*)'
        target_label: port
        replacement: '${2}'
```

**Prometheus startup flags**
```shell
--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels,metadata-wal-records
--web.enable-remote-write-receiver
--web.remote-write-receiver.accepted-protobuf-messages=io.prometheus.write.v2.Request
```

**Result**
```shell
[root@exp-01 grizzlybite]# curl -s 'http://192.168.100.7:9090/api/v1/query?query=node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes'  | jq '.data.result[0].metric'

{
  "__name__": "node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes",
  "__type__": "gauge",
  "instance": "test-node-exporter",
  "job": "node-exporter",
  "port": "9100"
}
```

---

### Case 2 - Prometheus Agent sends data via Remote Write v2
When Prometheus runs in **`--agent` mode** and sends metrics through **`remote_write`** using protobuf v2,  
the resulting metrics **do not contain** the `__type__` label - even with the same feature flags enabled.

**Prometheus (receiver)**
```shell
--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels,metadata-wal-records
--web.enable-remote-write-receiver
--web.remote-write-receiver.accepted-protobuf-messages=io.prometheus.write.v2.Request
```

**Prometheus Agent**
```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: "http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/write"
    protobuf_message: io.prometheus.write.v2.Request
    queue_config:
      max_shards: 40
      capacity: 10000
```

**Agent startup flags**
```shell
--agent
--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels,metadata-wal-records
```

**Result**
```shell
[root@exp-01 grizzlybite]# curl -s 'http://192.168.100.7:9090/api/v1/query?query=node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes'  | jq '.data.result[0].metric'
{
  "__name__": "node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes",
  "instance": "test-node-exporter",
  "job": "node-exporter",
  "port": "9100"
}
```

---

##  Summary
It looks like the `__type__` label is currently **not propagated** when metrics are sent via Prometheus Agent -> Prometheus using Remote Write v2, even though both sides have  
`--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels` enabled.

If this is the expected behavior (e.g., by design for the agent), please clarify.  
Otherwise, I’d be happy to help test any future fixes or patches!

---

**Environment**
- Prometheus 3.7.1
- node-exporter 1.9.1  
- Tested on AlmaLinux 9.6 (Sage Margay)
issue.author: grizzlybite

issue.title: OAuth2 authentication flows broken due to missing auth-signin annotation support in kubernetesIngressNginx provider
issue.body:
### Welcome!

- [x] Yes, I've searched similar issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/issues) and didn't find any.
- [x] Yes, I've searched similar issues on the [Traefik community forum](https://community.traefik.io) and didn't find any.


Migration: From NGINX Ingress Controller to Traefik

The kubernetesIngressNginx provider supports nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-url but does not support nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-signin, making OAuth2 authentication flows impossible to migrate from NGINX Ingress Controller. This creates a critical migration blocker for organizations with OAuth2-protected applications.

**Problem Statement**
OAuth2 authentication requires two essential components:
1. auth-url: Where to check authentication (supported)
2. auth-signin: Where to redirect unauthenticated users (NOT supported)

Without auth-signin, the authentication flow is incomplete.

**Current Behavior vs NGINX Ingress Controller**

**NGINX Ingress Controller (Working)**
```
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-url: "https://oauth2-proxy.team.com/oauth2/auth"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-signin: "https://oauth2-proxy.team.com/oauth2/start?rd=$scheme://$best_http_host$request_uri"
```
Result: Complete OAuth2 flow with proper redirects

**Traefik NGINX Provider (Broken)**
```
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-url: "https://oauth2-proxy.team.com/oauth2/auth"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-signin: "https://oauth2-proxy.team.com/oauth2/start?rd=$scheme://$best_http_host$request_uri"
```
Result:
1. auth-url triggers authentication (302 redirect)
2. auth-signin is ignored
3. OAuth2 flow breaks


**Technical Evidence**

**Test Configuration**
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: testapp
  namespace: test
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/force-ssl-redirect: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-signin: https://oauth2-proxy.team.com/oauth2/start?rd=$scheme://$best_http_host$request_uri
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-url: https://oauth2-proxy.team.com/oauth2/auth
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-response-headers: "X-Auth-Request-User,X-Auth-Request-Email"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx 
  rules:
    - host: test-example.team.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: whoami
                port:
                  number: 80
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - test-example.team.com
    secretName: team-cert
```

**HTTP Response (Showing Ignored auth-signin)**
```
HTTP/2 302 
content-type: text/html
location: https://oauth2-proxy.team.com/oauth2/start?rd=https://test-example.team.com/
accept-ranges: bytes
date: Wed, 31 Dec 2025 06:48:39 GMT
via: 1.1 varnish
x-served-by: cache-bom-vanm7210027-BOM
x-cache: MISS
x-cache-hits: 0
x-timer: S1767163719.309175,VS0,VE545
x-dbg-vcl2: bong_ke
strict-transport-security: max-age=300
content-length: 138
```

**The Core Issue: Incomplete OAuth2 Support**
The kubernetesIngressNginx provider currently implements partial OAuth2 support:

Result: Authentication starts but cannot complete successfully.

**Impact**
Migration Impossible: Cannot migrate OAuth2-protected applications
NGINX Retirement Deadline: March 2026 deadline cannot be met

**Problem**
Defeats the purpose of the NGINX provider for migration. 
Requires rewriting all Ingress configurations.

Suggested Implementation: Enable auth-signin Capability

### What does this PR do?

This PR adds minimal support for variable interpolation in the `auth-signin` NGINX annotation.
You can check the list of current available variables in the `interpolate.go` file (see https://github.com/traefik/traefik/pull/12640/changes#diff-9e1aaaea4b19f89501fac79971562bfafc05a0e50819e6f7947bf14768a859f4R10)

issue.title: Add a healthcheck endpoint
issue.body:
Hello! Wonderful project!

I am deploying Pocketbase to [Dokku](https://dokku.com/). It would be nice if there was a health-check/status endpoint that can be accessed without authorization. This could help in [zero-downtime](https://dokku.com/docs/deployment/zero-downtime-deploys/) deploys.
issue.author: IgnisDa

pr.title: Added health API endpoint
pr.body:
This PR adds an `/api/health` endpoint.

It responds with a `200 OK` status and adds the following body:

```
{
  "code": 200,
  "message": "API is healthy.",
  "status": "ok"
}
``` 

Everything except for the message is validated in a test. I think the message does not need to be tested, as others should not use it as a check (they should use the status code). Let me know if you see this differently, and I'll add the check.

fixes #1203
pr.author: MarvinJWendt

+package apis

issue.title: Add support for S3-compatible object-lock properties
issue.body:
Please see [this forum thread](https://forum.rclone.org/t/requesting-support-for-s3-compatible-object-lock-properties/19675) for initial details including links to the API calls supported by both AWS and Backblaze.

Currently AWS and Backblaze (via their S3 API only) support object immutability. I am proposing a set of flags which would leverage this feature in supported object storage systems. A brief (and probably incomplete) overview of suggested flags follows:

### At bucket creation
` --s3-bucket-object-lock-enabled` - for "rclone mkdir" this enables object-locking for a bucket. It's important to note this _must_ be set at the time a bucket is created for objects inside that bucket to be lockable.

### At object creation/upload
`--s3-object-lock-mode` [GOVERNANCE|COMPLIANCE]
`--s3-object-lock-retain-until-date` [date]
`--s3-object-lock-retention-period` [days]
`--s3-object-lock-legal-hold` [ON|OFF] default off

### At object deletion
` --s3-bypass-governance-retention`

### Determine lock status
`rclone backend list-object-lock`

Additionally, the configurator for S3 would need to know about this feature and which APIs support it so a user would get big scary warnings if they tried to set object-locking in an incompatible provider. This probably means Backblaze should be added to the S3 configurator in addition to the current native B2 configuration.
issue.author: taupehat

pr.title: s3: add Object Lock support
pr.body:
#### What is the purpose of this change?

Add comprehensive S3 Object Lock support with the following new options:

- `--s3-object-lock-mode`: Set Object Lock mode (GOVERNANCE/COMPLIANCE/copy)
- `--s3-object-lock-retain-until-date`: Set retention date (RFC3339/duration/copy)
- `--s3-object-lock-legal-hold-status`: Set legal hold (ON/OFF/copy)
- `--s3-bypass-governance-retention`: Bypass governance mode for deletions
- `--s3-bucket-object-lock-enabled`: Enable Object Lock when creating buckets
- `--s3-object-lock-set-after-upload`: Set retention via separate API calls

The special value `copy` preserves the source object's setting when used with `--metadata`, enabling scenarios like cloning from COMPLIANCE to GOVERNANCE while keeping the original retention date.


#### Was the change discussed in an issue or in the forum before?

Fixes #4683
See also #7894, #7893, #8866

#### The associated forum post URL from `https://forum.rclone.org`



#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

Path elements that contain a SEMICOLON  (`;`) are truncated.  The SEMICOLON and any characters after it within a path element are missing. 

#### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`)

```console
paul@monkeywrench:~$ rclone version
rclone v1.73.0-beta.9373.28c187b9b
- os/version: debian 12.12 (64 bit)
- os/kernel: 6.1.0-41-amd64 (x86_64)

- go/linking: dynamic
- go/tags: none
paul@monkeywrench:~$ 
```

#### Which OS you are using and how many bits (e.g. Windows 7, 64 bit)

```console
paul@monkeywrench:~$ lsb_release -a
No LSB modules are available.
Distributor ID: Debian
Description:    Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)
Release:        12
Codename:       bookworm
paul@monkeywrench:~$ 
```

#### Which cloud storage system are you using? (e.g. Google Drive)

dCache (`466b32883f`, current tip from `master` branch).

#### The command you were trying to run (e.g. `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

```console
paul@monkeywrench:~$ rclone copy /bin/bash 'dcache-systemtest:public/my;test'
paul@monkeywrench:~$ rclone ls 'dcache-systemtest:public'
  1265648 my/bash
paul@monkeywrench:~$ 
```

#### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag (e.g. output from `rclone -vv copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

```console
paul@monkeywrench:~$ rclone -vv copy /bin/bash 'dcache-systemtest:public/my;test'
2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : rclone: Version "v1.73.0-beta.9373.28c187b9b" starting with parameters ["rclone" "-vv" "copy" "/bin/bash" "dcache-systemtest:public/my;test"]
2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : Creating backend with remote "/bin/bash"
2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : Using config file from "/home/paul/.config/rclone/rclone.conf"
2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : fs cache: renaming child cache item "/bin/bash" to be canonical for parent "/bin"
2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : Creating backend with remote "dcache-systemtest:public/my;test"
2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : found headers: 
2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : bash: Need to transfer - File not found at Destination
2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : bash: Update will use the normal upload strategy (no chunks)
2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : bash: size = 1265648 OK
2026/01/07 11:19:06 INFO  : bash: Copied (new)
2026/01/07 11:19:06 INFO  : 
Transferred:        1.207 MiB / 1.207 MiB, 100%, 0 B/s, ETA -
Transferred:            1 / 1, 100%
Elapsed time:         0.1s

2026/01/07 11:19:06 DEBUG : 7 go routines active
paul@monkeywrench:~$ 
```

<!--- Please keep the note below for others who read your bug report. -->

#### Additional context and information.

I believe I understand the problem.

rclone is making requests with paths containing unescaped SEMICOLON characters.

dCache (actually Jetty) is interpreting an unescaped SEMICOLON as "scheme-specific or dereference-handler-specific subcomponents within a path segment".  See [Jetty issue 2067](https://github.com/jetty/jetty.project/issues/2067) for a briefly discusses on this.  The issue points to [RFC 3986 §3.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-3.3) describing how reserved characters _must_ be escaped if intended to be a literal value.

[RFC 4918 §3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4918#section-3) describes path segments in WebDAV, but defers the definition to RFC 3986 §3.3.

So, it appears that rclone is not conforming with RFC 3986 by expecting the WebDAV server to accept unescaped semicolons (within a path segment) as a literal semicolon character in that path element.  It may by fine for some WebDAV servers, but I suggest that's "works by accident".

In the rclone code, confusion seems to arise from the WebDAV backend [using URLPathEscape](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/5f4e4b1a200708f5f36999a9d289823b742e4fd3/backend/webdav/webdav.go#L426).  The [URLPathEscape function](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/5f4e4b1a200708f5f36999a9d289823b742e4fd3/lib/rest/url.go#L23) uses go's standard URL support (`url.URL`) by calling `String()` function.

If I've understood `String` correctly, this function provides minimal escaping of the URL's path (I think, only `?`).  Reserved characters (such as SEMICOLON) are not escaped.

I believe this issue is actually part of a larger issue, where other reserved characters are not being escaped.  I've confirmed that EQUALS (`=`) also appears unescaped in path segments, despite being a reserved character.

pr.title: webdav: use URLPathEscapeAll for RFC 3986 compliant path encoding
pr.body:
Fixes #9082

The WebDAV backend uses `URLPathEscape` for path encoding, which relies on Go's `url.URL.String()`. This only does minimal escaping and lets reserved sub-delimiter characters like semicolons (`;`) and equals signs (`=`) through unescaped.

Per RFC 3986 section 3.3, these characters must be percent-encoded when used as literal path values. Some WebDAV servers (dCache running on Jetty in the reporter's case) interpret unescaped semicolons as path parameter delimiters per the RFC, which silently truncates the filename at the semicolon position.

Switched to `URLPathEscapeAll` which encodes everything except `[A-Za-z0-9/]`. As @ncw mentioned in the issue, the extra encoding overhead is negligible compared to data transfer and round trips.

Added a test that spins up a mock WebDAV server and verifies semicolons in filenames are percent-encoded in the request path.

 	}

+	return rest.URLPathEscapeAll(subPath)

@@ -80,3 +80,35 @@ func TestHeaders(t *testing.T) {

 	require.NoError(t, err)
 }
+
+// TestReservedCharactersInPathAreEscaped verifies that reserved characters
+// like semicolons and equals signs in file paths are percent-encoded in
+// HTTP requests to the WebDAV server (RFC 3986 compliance).
+func TestReservedCharactersInPathAreEscaped(t *testing.T) {
+	var capturedPath string
+
+	handler := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		capturedPath = r.RequestURI
+		// Return a 404 so the NewObject call fails cleanly
+		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
+	})
+	ts := httptest.NewServer(handler)
+	defer ts.Close()
+
+	configfile.Install()
+	m := configmap.Simple{
+		"type": "webdav",
+		"url":  ts.URL,
+	}
+
+	f, err := webdav.NewFs(context.Background(), remoteName, "", m)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// Try to access a file with a semicolon in the name.
+	// We expect the request to fail (404), but the path should be escaped.
+	_, _ = f.NewObject(context.Background(), "my;test")
+
+	// The semicolon must be percent-encoded as %3B
+	assert.Contains(t, capturedPath, "my%3Btest", "semicolons in path should be percent-encoded")
+	assert.NotContains(t, capturedPath, "my;test", "raw semicolons should not appear in path")
+}

pr.title: Replace `olivere/elastic` with REST API client, add OpenSearch support
pr.body:
Drops `github.com/olivere/elastic/v7` (unmaintained) and replaces it with a small in-house wrapper that speaks the Elasticsearch REST API directly via `net/http`. The subset used by Gitea (`_cluster/health`, `_bulk`, `_doc`, `_delete_by_query`, `_refresh`, `_search`, `HEAD`/`PUT` index) is stable across the targeted servers, so no client library is needed.

**Targets tested**
- Elasticsearch 7, 8, 9
- OpenSearch 1, 2, 3

**Why not `go-elasticsearch`?**
The official client enforces an `X-Elastic-Product` server-identity check that OpenSearch deliberately fails, which would force shipping a transport shim to defeat it. Going direct over `net/http` removes that fight along with several MB of transitive deps (`elastic-transport-go`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel{,/metric,/trace}`, `auto/sdk`, `easyjson`, `intern`, `logr`, `stdr`).

Replaces: #30755
Fixes: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/30752

---
This PR was written with the help of Claude Opus 4.7
